recommended_estimator.candidate_clean_unmapped_file_bytes: C = max(0, min(max(0, file-shmem), active_file+inactive_file) - file_mapped - file_dirty - file_writeback - unevictable)
recommended_estimator.unlimited_cgroup_rule: Use host_MemAvailable only when memory.max=max; do not add cache credit to it
recommended_estimator.missing_or_invalid_required_counters: Fail closed; do not replace unknown counters with zero
recommended_estimator.half_credit_status: Prospective policy haircut fixed before any scientific worker; not a kernel guarantee, fitted probability or proven lower bound

reasoning: Active and unevictable are different LRU classifications. Primary documentation and kernel source allow eligible active file folios to be deactivated and reclaimed; inactive-only counting can omit usable clean file cache.

The type-based file counter includes shmem while file LRU counters classify pages differently. Taking the minimum with non-shmem file avoids treating shmem or unrelated file accounting as an additional reclaim credit.

Subtracting mapped, dirty, writeback and unevictable amounts excludes or conservatively over-excludes categories with additional reclaim obstacles. These counters can overlap; the subtraction is an intentionally pessimistic estimate, not an exact disjoint-set decomposition.
The fixed50percent haircut leaves half of the estimated candidate cache uncredited. It is an explicit resource policy margin independent of the amount needed to pass today's threshold.

The host MemAvailable cap is another estimate and prevents adding cgroup cache credit to a host-level figure that already contains cache availability. Signed cgroup headroom must be added before the final zero clamp.

The estimate does not establish that any specified bytes will actually be freed, immediately or before allocation pressure. Fresh admission, worker RLIMIT_AS, actual receipts and failure preservation remain necessary.
limitations: Clean unmapped active file cache may still have transient references, pins, filesystem constraints or hot working-set demand. The counters do not identify every obstacle.

Unevictable documentation explicitly allows some not-yet-culled unevictable folios to remain temporarily on ordinary active/inactive lists; subtracting the unevictable counter cannot prove their absence.
Counters are not an atomic snapshot; parallel allocations, writeback and LRU transitions may change the situation after admission.
Reclaim may cause refaults, CPU or I/O latency. No kernel background CPU or reclaim-time bound is inferred.
The host version string matches the fetched stable tag, but running kernel build configuration, custom patches and enabled reclaim path are not independently identified.
A50percent policy allowance is not an outward lower bound on immediately allocatable memory. No hard memory or aggregate CPU safety proof is claimed.
The old failed memory gate is not retroactively converted to PASS; only a separately frozenv2 context may be evaluated.
